CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE N2M25-24

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE ALHAMBRA HOUSING AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE

  TUESDAY, March 4, 2025
  6:30 PM

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a regular meeting of the Alhambra Housing and
Community Development Citizen Advisory (HCDA) Committee will be held on Tuesday,
March 4, 2025, commencing at 6:30 pm, at Alhambra City Hall, Conference Room
A, 2nd Floor, 111 South First Street, Alhambra CA, pursuant to the order of the
Chairman of the HCDA Committee, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal
Code, and Section 54596 of the Government Code of the State of California.

  ESTEBAN ALVAREZ, MANAGEMENT ANALYST
  HCDA COMMITTEE SECRETARY

Dated: February 27, 2025
  Notice No: N2M25-24
   AGENDA

HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  TUESDAY, March 4, 2025, 6:30 PM

  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA CITY HALL
  CONFERENCE ROOM A
  111 SOUTH FIRST STREET
  ALHAMBRA, CA 91801

1. ROLL CALL:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair  Andrea Giese
  Lewis McCammon, Vice Chair  Bonita Sharma-Ngan
  Marc Tousignant  Yvette Cardenas
  Michael Soto  Renee-Marie Alvarez

2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES: 9/5/2023; 5/7/2024; 9/3/2024; 12/3/2024;
  2/4/2025

3. PROGRESS REPORTS - Attached for the Committee’s review are copies of the
  Progress Reports for those programs utilizing Community Development Block
  Grant and HOME Funds. All figures indicate the progress made and services
  rendered to date for FY 2024-2025.

  a. Parks and Recreation: Senior Case Management
  i. Case Management Clients Served: 88
  ii. Volunteer Hours of assistance donated: 33
  iii. Meals delivered: 3086
  iv. Telephone calls made: 730
  b. Community Development: Code Enforcement
  i. Total number of complaints investigated: 382
  ii. Number of complaints identified as Health and Safety: 74
  iii. Number of referrals to the Housing Dept programs: 20
  c. Community Development: Housing Rights Center
  i. Number of clients served (approximately): 271
  ii. A variety of issues were discussed including evictions, security
  deposits, rent increases, repairs, contract questions, etc.
  d. Community Development: Home Improvement Programs
  i. HOME Major Rehabilitation: 3 in progress, 1 completed, 1
  cancelled
  ii. CDBG Minor Rehabilitation: 4 in progress, 1 completed, 1
  cancelled

  Recommended Action: Receive and file informational reports.

4. WORKING MEETING IN PREPARATION OF THE 2025-2029 CONSOLIDATED
  PLAN AND 2025-26 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN
   The City is required by the Department of Housing and Urban Development to
  prepare a “Consolidated Plan” and Annual Action Plans. The Consolidated Plan
  identifies the City’s programs funded with Housing and Urban Development
  Funds and the community’s needs over the next five years. This working
  meeting/discussion by the HCDA will focus on eligible CDBG and HOME
  activities and propose new or other funding recommendations under CDBG and
  HOME. Community organizations have been invited to participate in the meeting
  to give input on community development needs and fair housing issues in the
  City. Committee and public comments received will be considered as the City
  drafts its program plans for the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and the 2025-26
  Annual Action Plan.

  Recommended Action: Receive public comments and direct staff to include all
  comments received for consideration with the DRAFT 2025-2029 Consolidated
  Plan and 2025-26 Action Plan.

  5. STAFF UPDATES
  Discussion from the Staff Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda.
  Items discussed must pertain the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory
  Committee.

  6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  Discussion from the public of any items not specified on the agenda. Comments
  must pertain to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee. Public
  comments pertaining to the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee’s business are
  welcome. Kindly limit all oral communications to five (5) minutes. Please
  complete a speak card prior to the meeting and submit the card to the
  Committee’s Secretary.

  7. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the
  agenda. Items discussed must pertain the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory
  Committee.

  8. ADJOURNMENT

Copies of the staff report or other written documentation relating to each item of
business described herein are on file in the Office of Management Services, Alhambra
City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, CA, and are available for public inspection
during regular office hours from 7:00 am to 5:30: PM, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior the
meeting, the person may contact Esteban Alvarez in the Management Services
Department in person at City Hall or at 626.570.5012 during regular business hours.

    OFFICIAL
  Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of December 3, 2024
  CITY HALL • 111 S. FIRST ST.

  Committee Chair Vallejos called the meeting to order at 6:34 pm.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair  Lewis McCammon, Vice Chair
  Bonita Sharma-Ngan  Yvette Cardenas
  Marc Tousignant  Renee-Marie Alvarez
  Andrea Giese

  Committee Members Absent:
  Bonita Sharma-Ngan
  Michael Soto

  City Staff Present:
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager
  Esteban Alvarez, Management Analyst

2. INTRODUCTION

  Committee Member Renee-Marie Alvarez was introduced as the newest HCDA Committee
  Member.

4. PROGRESS REPORTS

  Management Analyst Esteban Alvarez presented the committee with progress reports
  covering the period from July 1, 2024, to October 31, 2024, for the Senior Case
  Management, Code Enforcement, Housing Rights Center, and Home Improvement
  Programs. Staff requested that the reports be received and filed by the committee.

  Committee Action:

  The Committee received and filed these informational reports.

5. Kickoff of Five-Year Consolidated Plan (2025-2029) and Annual Action Plan -
  Presentation by consultant Erin Lay from Veronica Tam and Associates, Inc.

  Committee Member Cardenas inquired whether the anticipated numbers for CDBG and
  HOME funding should be more conservative, given the new federal administration.
  Consultant Lay explained that it is standard practice to use the current funding numbers for
  CDBG and HOME until the actual figures are released. However, Lay acknowledged that
  funding levels may change under the new administration.

  Vice Chair McCammon requested that the PowerPoint presentation by Erin Lay be posted
  online for public access.

  Page 1 of 2
   Management Analyst Esteban Alvarez informed the committee that staff is planning a
  February 2025 meeting to provide a more detailed review of the Five-Year Consolidated Plan
  and Annual Action Plan.

  A member of the public, Marlene Bronson, expressed interest in speaking during the
  presentation portion of the meeting. Chair Vallejos requested that her comments be saved for
  the 'Comments from the Audience' section of the meeting.

  Committee Action:

  Information report, no action required.

6. STAFF UPDATES: CHDO Bulletin: Reprogram HOME Major Rehabilitation

  Assistant City Manager Lucy Garcia presented an updated CHDO Bulletin to the committee.

7. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE

  Marlene Bronson attended the meeting to share concerns about her mother’s 1999 HUD-
  funded home, which faced issues with the contractor and materials during rehabilitation. She
  explained that she wasn’t given the option to choose the contractor, resulting in unresolved
  litigation and the loss of an antique fireplace. Despite these challenges, she noted that her
  mother’s home is now in good condition.

8. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE

  Vice Chair McCammon asked if CDBG funds could be used to hire a staff member for fair
  housing activities, such as tenant and landlord counseling, instead of relying on the Housing
  Rights Center. He also suggested revisiting a previous reporting model for code enforcement
  that highlights complaints and actions in low- and moderate-income areas.

  Committee Member Cardenas proposed holding a standing monthly meeting, eliminating the
  need for a quorum poll. Chair Vallejos emphasized the importance of confirming a quorum
  in advance to respect everyone's time.

  The Committee requested that Holly Chenh, Housing Assistant, present on the Home
  Rehabilitation program and clarify whether funds for rehabilitation must be repaid if a
  homeowner sells the property.

9. ADJOURNMENT: 7:30 p.m.

  Motion to adjourn the meeting made by Chair Vallejos and seconded by Vice Chair
  McCammon. The motion was approved unanimously by all committee members.

BACKGROUND

To receive CDBG and HOME funds, the City must prepare:

 • Consolidated Plan every five years to establish funding priorities
  v  v
 • Annual Action Plans to outline specific actions and goals

 • Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice

 GOALS OF CDBG AND HOME PROGRAMS
  • Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) - develop viable urban
  communities, principally for persons of low- and-moderate income by:
  •  Providing decent housing;
  •  Creating a suitable living environment; and
  •  Expanding
  v  economic opportunities.  v
  • HOME Investment Partnership (HOME) – preserve and create
  affordable housing for low- and moderate-income households.

Program statutes and regulations set forth eligible activities, goals, and
program spending caps.
   6

WHAT IS THE CONSOLIDATED PLAN (CP)?

• Required to receive funds from HUD
• Five-year plan guiding use of HUD funds, containing
  • Housing and community needs assessment
  • Strategic plan
  v
  • Market analysis  v
  • Priorities and goals
  • First-year Annual Action Plan (Subsequent Annual Action Plans done separately
  for years two through five)
   7

USE OF HUD FUNDS

All CDBG activities/programs must meet a National Objective
  1. Benefit low- and moderate-income persons
  2. Eliminate slums and blight

households
